units.rightText: lest they drink and forget what is decreed, depriving all the oppressed of justice. Give strong drink to one who is perishing, and wine to the bitter in soul.

units.leftText: Let him drink, and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more. Open your mouth for the mute, in the cause of all who are left desolate.
units.rightText: Let him drink and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more. Open your mouth for those with no voice, for the cause of all the dispossessed.

units.leftText: Open your mouth, judge righteously, and serve justice to the poor and needy.” Who can find a worthy woman? For her value is far above rubies.
units.rightText: Open your mouth, judge righteously, and defend the cause of the poor and needy. The Virtues of a Noble Woman A wife of noble character, who can find? She is far more precious than rubies.

units.leftText: The heart of her husband trusts in her. He shall have no lack of gain. She does him good, and not harm, all the days of her life.
units.rightText: The heart of her husband trusts in her, and he lacks nothing of value. She brings him good and not harm all the days of her life.

units.leftText: She seeks wool and flax, and works eagerly with her hands. She is like the merchant ships. She brings her bread from afar.
units.rightText: She selects wool and flax and works with eager hands. She is like the merchant ships, bringing her food from afar.

units.leftText: She rises also while it is yet night, gives food to her household, and portions for her servant girls. She considers a field, and buys it. With the fruit of her hands, she plants a vineyard.
units.rightText: She rises while it is still night to provide food for her household and portions for her maidservants. She appraises a field and buys it; from her earnings she plants a vineyard.

units.leftText: She arms her waist with strength, and makes her arms strong. She perceives that her merchandise is profitable. Her lamp doesn’t go out by night.
units.rightText: She girds herself with strength and shows that her arms are strong. She sees that her gain is good, and her lamp is not extinguished at night.

units.leftText: She lays her hands to the distaff, and her hands hold the spindle. She opens her arms to the poor; yes, she extends her hands to the needy.
units.rightText: She stretches out her hands to the distaff and grasps the spindle with her fingers. She opens her arms to the poor and reaches out her hands to the needy.

units.leftText: She is not afraid of the snow for her household, for all her household are clothed with scarlet. She makes for herself carpets of tapestry. Her clothing is fine linen and purple.
units.rightText: When it snows, she has no fear for her household, for they are all clothed in scarlet. She makes coverings for her bed; her clothing is fine linen and purple.

units.leftText: Her husband is respected in the gates, when he sits among the elders of the land. She makes linen garments and sells them, and delivers sashes to the merchant.
units.rightText: Her husband is known at the city gates, where he sits among the elders of the land. She makes linen garments and sells them; she delivers sashes to the merchants.

units.leftText: Strength and dignity are her clothing. She laughs at the time to come. She opens her mouth with wisdom. Kind instruction is on her tongue.
units.rightText: Strength and honor are her clothing, and she can laugh at the days to come. She opens her mouth with wisdom, and faithful instruction is on her tongue.

units.leftText: She looks well to the ways of her household, and doesn’t eat the bread of idleness. Her children rise up and call her blessed. Her husband also praises her:
units.rightText: She watches over the affairs of her household and does not eat the bread of idleness. Her children rise up and call her blessed; her husband praises her as well:

units.leftText: “Many women do noble things, but you excel them all.” Charm is deceitful, and beauty is vain; but a woman who fears the LORD, she shall be praised.
units.rightText: “Many daughters have done noble things, but you surpass them all!” Charm is deceptive and beauty is fleeting, but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.
